19.27: Don't cut your hair on the sides of your head or trim the sides of your beard,
19.28: don't cut your bodies in some pagan ritual for the dead, and don't get yourselves tattoos. I am the Lord.
19.29: Don't bring shame on your daughter by making her a prostitute, otherwise the land will become morally and spiritually depraved.
19.30: Keep my Sabbaths and show respect for my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
19.31: Don't try and find help from mediums or spiritists—don't even go looking for them, otherwise they will corrupt you. I am the Lord your God.
19.32: Stand up and be respectful of older people. Show reverence for your God. I am the Lord.
19.33: Don't mistreat foreigners who live in your country.
19.34: Treat them in the same way as a fellow citizen, and love them as you love yourself, because you were once foreigners living in Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
19.35: Don't use dishonest weights and measures.
19.36: Make sure your scales and weights are accurate, that your measures of ephah and hin are correct. I am the Lord your God who led you out of Egypt.
19.37: Keep all my rules and regulations, and make sure you follow them. I am the Lord.”

20.2: “Tell the Israelites: These regulations are for both Israelites and foreigners living among them. Anyone who sacrifices their children to Molech must be executed. The community must stone them to death.
20.3: I will disown them and expel them from their people, because by sacrificing their children to Molech they have polluted my sanctuary and disgraced my reputation.
20.4: If the community decides to look the other way and not execute those who sacrifice their children to Molech, then I will take action against them myself.
20.5: I will disown them and their family, and expel them from their people—and not just them, but everyone who follows them in spiritually prostituting themselves with Molech.
20.6: I will also disown and expel from their people anyone who goes to mediums or spiritists and in this way commits spiritual prostitution with them.
20.7: So dedicate yourselves and be holy, because I am the Lord your God.
20.8: Keep my rules and put them into practice. I am the Lord who makes you holy.
20.9: Anyone who curses their father or mother must be executed. They have cursed their father or mother; they bear the responsibility for their punishment.
20.10: Any man who commits adultery with someone else's wife must be executed, as well as the woman.
20.11: A man who has sex with his father's wife has brought shame on his father .Both the man and the woman must be executed. Both must surely be put to death; they bear the responsibility for their punishment.
20.12: A man who has sex with his daughter-in-law must be executed, as well as the woman. They have done something perverse; they bear the responsibility for their punishment.
20.13: Men who have sex with other men as with a woman have done something disgusting. They must be executed; they bear the responsibility for their punishment.
20.14: A man who marries both a woman and her mother has acted perversely. They must all be burned to death so that there will be no such wickedness among you.
20.15: A man who has sex with an animal must be executed, and the animal must be killed too.
20.16: A woman who gives herself to an animal to have sex with it must be executed, along with the animal. They must both be killed; they bear the responsibility for their punishment.
20.17: A man who marries his sister ,whether she's his father's daughter or his mother's daughter ,and they have sex, has done something shameful. They must be expelled from their people in front of everybody. He has brought shame on his sister; he bears the responsibility for his punishment.
20.18: A man who has sex with a woman having her period has exposed where her blood flow comes from, and she has too. They must both be expelled from their people.
20.19: Don't have sex with your aunt, whether on your father's or your mother's side, because it brings shame on your own family. Both will bear responsibility for their sin.
20.20: A man who has sex with his uncle's wife brings shame on his uncle. They will bear responsibility for their sin; they shall die without having children.
20.21: A man who marries his brother's wife does something that is unclean. He has brought shame on his brother; the couple will have no children.
20.22: So keep all my rules and regulations, so that the land where I'm taking you to live won't vomit you out.
20.23: Don't follow the practices of the nations I'm expelling for you. I detested them because they did all these evil things.
20.24: But I have promised you that you will take over their land. I'm going to give it to you to own, a land that flows with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, who has made you a distinctive people different from all others.
20.25: So make sure you observe the difference between clean and unclean animals and birds. Don't make yourselves unclean because of any animal or bird, or by anything that runs along the ground. I have made the difference clear: they are unclean for you.
20.26: You shall be holy to me because I am holy. I am the Lord, and I have made you a distinctive people different from all other nations. You belong to me.
20.27: Anyone, man or woman, who is a medium or a spiritist must be executed. They are to be stoned to death; they bear the responsibility for their punishment.”

21.1: The Lord told Moses, “Tell Aaron's sons, the priests: A priest is not to make himself unclean by touching the dead body of any of his relatives.
21.2: The only exceptions are for his immediate family. This includes his mother , father ,son, daughter ,or brother ,
21.3: or his unmarried sister since she is a close relative because she doesn't have a husband.
21.4: He must not make himself unclean for those only related to him by marriage—he is not to make himself ceremonially impure.
21.5: Priests are not to shave bald spots on their heads, trim the sides of their beards, or cut their bodies.
21.6: They must be holy to their God and not disgrace their God's reputation. They are the ones who present the food offerings to the Lord, the food of their God. Consequently they must be holy.
21.7: A priest is not to marry a woman made unclean through prostitution or who is divorced by her husband, for the priest must be holy to his God.
21.8: You shall consider him holy because he presents the food offerings to your God. He shall be holy to you, because I am holy. I am the Lord, and I chose you as my special people.
21.9: A priest's daughter who makes herself unclean through prostitution makes her father unclean. She must be executed by burning.
21.10: The high priest has the highest place among the other priests. He has been anointed with olive oil poured on his head and has been ordained to wear the priestly clothing. He must not leave his hair uncombed or tear his clothes.
21.11: He is not to go near any dead body. He must not make himself unclean, even if it is for his own father or mother .
21.12: He must not leave to deal with someone who has died or make the sanctuary of his God unclean because he has been dedicated by the anointing oil of his God. I am the Lord.
21.13: He can only marry a virgin.
21.14: He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or one made unclean through prostitution. He has to marry a virgin from his own people,
21.15: so that he doesn't make his children unclean among his people, for I am the Lord who makes him holy.”
21.17: “Tell Aaron: These rules apply for all future generations. If any of your descendants has a physical defect, he is not allowed to come and present the food offerings of his God.
21.18: No man is allowed to do this if he has any defects, including anyone who is blind, crippled, facially disfigured, or has deformities,
21.19: anyone who has a broken foot or arm,
21.20: anyone who is a hunchback or dwarf, or who has cataracts, skin sores or scabs, or a damaged testicle.
21.21: No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect is allowed to come and present the food offerings to the Lord. Because he has a defect, he must not come and offer the food of his God.
21.22: He is still allowed to eat the food from the Most Holy Place of his God and also from the sanctuary,
21.23: but because he has a defect, he is not allowed to go near the curtain or the altar , so that my sanctuary and everything in it are not made unclean, because I am the Lord who makes them holy.”
21.24: Moses repeated this to Aaron and his sons, and to all the Israelites.

22.2: “Tell Aaron and his sons to be dedicated when dealing with the holy offerings that the Israelites have dedicated to me, so that they don't dishonor my holy character .I am the Lord.
22.3: Tell them: These rules apply for all future generations. If any of your descendants in an unclean state comes close to the holy offerings that the Israelites dedicate to honor the Lord, that person must be expelled from my presence. I am the Lord.
22.4: If one of Aaron's descendants has a skin disease or a discharge, he is not allowed to eat the holy offerings until he is clean. Anyone who touches anything made unclean by a dead body or by a man who has had a release of semen,
22.5: or anyone who touches an unclean animal or an unclean person (whatever the uncleanness is), leave the sanctuary.
22.6: anyone who touches anything like this will remain unclean until evening. He is not allowed to eat from the holy offerings unless he has washed himself with water .
22.7: At sunset he will become clean, and then he is allowed to eat from the holy offerings because they provide his food.
22.8: He must not eat anything that has died, or has been killed by wild animals, because that would make him unclean. I am the Lord.
22.9: The priests must do as I demand, so that they don't become guilty and die because they have not done so, treating my requirements with contempt. I am the Lord who makes them holy.
22.10: Anyone who isn't part of a priest's family is not allowed to eat the holy offerings. This also applies to a priest's guest or his paid worker .
22.11: However ,if a priest uses his own money to buy a slave, or if a slave is born in the priest's household, then that slave is allowed to eat his food.
22.12: If the priest's daughter gets married to a man who isn't a priest, she is not allowed to eat the holy offerings.
22.13: But if a priest's daughter without children is widowed or divorced and goes back to her father's house, she is allowed to eat her father's food as she did when she was growing up. But no one outside the priest's family can eat it.
22.14: Anyone who eats a holy offering by mistake must pay compensation by adding a fifth to its value, and give it all to the priest.
22.15: The priests must not make the holy offerings the Israelites present to the Lord unclean
22.16: by allowing the people to eat them and in so doing take upon themselves the punishment for guilt. For I am the Lord who makes them holy.”
22.18: “Tell Aaron, his sons and all the Israelites: If you or a foreigner living with you wants to make a gift as a burnt offering to the Lord, whether it's to fulfill a promise or as a freewill offering, this is what you are to do.
22.19: If it is to be accepted on your behalf you must offer a male without defects from the herds of cattle, sheep, or goats.
22.20: Don't present anything with a defect because it won't be accepted on your behalf.
22.21: If you want to present a peace offering to the Lord from the herd or flock to fulfill a promise or as a freewill offering, in order to be acceptable the animal must be perfect, completely without defects.
22.22: Don't present to the Lord an animal that is blind, injured, or damaged in some way, or has warts, skin sores, or scabs. Don't place any animal that has these on the altar as a food offering to the Lord.
22.23: However ,you can present a freewill offering of a bull or sheep that has a leg that is too long or too short, but not if it is a sacrifice to fulfill a promise.
22.24: Don't present to the Lord an animal with testicles that are accidentally or deliberately damaged. You are not allowed to sacrifice any of these damaged animals in your land.
22.25: Nor are you allowed to accept such animals from a foreigner that are damaged and defective.”
22.27: “When a bull, a sheep, or a goat is born, it must stay with its mother for seven days. After eight days it can be accepted as a food offering to the Lord.
22.28: However ,don't kill a bull or a sheep and its young on the same day.
22.29: When you present a thank offering to the Lord, make sure to do so in a way that it will be accepted on your behalf.
22.30: It has to be eaten on the same day. Don't leave any of it until morning. I am the Lord.
22.31: Keep my rules and put them into practice. I am the Lord.
22.32: Don't disgrace my holy character .I must be accepted as holy by you. I am the Lord who makes you holy.
22.33: I am the one who led you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.”

23.2: “Tell the Israelites that these are my religious festivals, the festivals of the Lord that you are to call as the holy times when we meet together .
23.3: You have six days to work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy day of meeting together .Don't do any work. It is the Lord's Sabbath everywhere you live.
23.4: These are the Lord's religious festivals, the holy meetings that you are to announce at their specific times.
23.5: The Lord's Passover starts on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
23.6: The Lord's Festival of Unleavened Bread begins on the fifteenth day of the first month. For seven days the bread you eat must be made without yeast.
23.7: On the first day you are to hold a holy meeting. You must not do any of your usual work.
23.8: For seven days you shall present food offerings to the Lord. There is to be a holy meeting on the seventh day. You must not do any of your usual work.”
23.10: “Tell the Israelites that when you enter the land that I'm giving you and you harvest your crops, take a stack of grain from the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest.
23.11: He will wave the stack of grain before the Lord so that it may be accepted on your behalf. The priest is to do this the day following the Sabbath.
23.12: When you wave the stack of grain, you are to present a one-year-old lamb without defects as a burnt offering to the Lord,
23.13: together with its grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of the best flour mixed with olive oil (a food offering to the Lord to be accepted by him) and its drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.
23.14: Don't eat any bread, roasted grain, or new grain until the time you bring this offering to your God. This regulation is for all time and for future generations everywhere you live.
23.15: Count seven full weeks from the day after the Sabbath—the day you brought the stack of grain as a wave offering.
23.16: Count fifty days until the day after the seventh Sabbath, and on that day present an offering of new grain to the Lord.
23.17: Bring two loaves of bread from your homes as a wave offering. Make them from two-tenths of an ephah of the best flour ,baked with yeast, as the firstfruits to the Lord.
23.18: As well as the bread, present seven one-year-old male lambs without defects, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the Lord, as well as their grain offerings and drink offerings, a food offering to the Lord to be accepted by him.
23.19: Present one male goat as a sin offering and two one-year-old male lambs as a peace offering.
23.20: The priest will wave the lambs as a wave offering before the Lord, along with the bread of the firstfruits. The bread and the two lambs are holy to the Lord and belong to the priest.
23.21: That same day you are to announce a holy meeting, and you must not do any of your usual work. This regulation is for all time and for future generations everywhere you live.
23.22: When you harvest the crops grown on your land, don't harvest right up to the edges of your field, or collect what has been missed. Leave them for the poor people and foreigners. I am the Lord your God.”
23.24: “Tell the Israelites that on the first day of the seventh month you are to have a special Sabbath of complete rest, a holy meeting that is announced by the sound of trumpets.
23.25: Don't do any of your usual work; instead you are to present a food offering to the Lord.”
23.27: “The Day of Atonement is on the tenth day of this seventh month. You are to have a holy meeting, deny yourselves, and present a food offering to the Lord
23.28: On this day you must not do any of your usual work because it is the Day of Atonement, when things are made right for you before the Lord your God.
23.29: Anyone who does not practice self-denial on this day must be expelled from their people.
23.30: I will destroy anyone of you who does any work on this day.
23.31: Don't do any kind of work at all. This regulation is for all time and for future generations everywhere you live.
23.32: It is to be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall practice self-denial. You are to observe your Sabbath from the evening of the ninth day of the month until evening the next day.”
23.34: “Tell the Israelites that the Feast of Tabernacles to honor the Lord begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and lasts for seven days.
23.35: On the first day have a holy meeting. You must not do any of your usual work.
23.36: For seven days you shall present food offerings to the Lord. On the eighth day you are to have another holy meeting and present a food offering to the Lord. It is a meeting for worship. You must not do any of your usual work.
23.37: These are the Lord's holy festivals, which you are to announce as holy meetings for presenting food offerings to the Lord. These include burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each according to the specific day.
23.38: All of these offerings are in addition to those for the Lord's Sabbaths. They are also in addition to your gifts, to all your offerings to fulfill promises, and to all the freewill offerings you present to the Lord.
23.39: You shall celebrate a feast to honor the Lord for seven days on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, once you have harvested your crops. The first day and the eighth day are Sabbaths of complete rest.
23.40: On the first day you are to gather branches from large trees, from palm trees, from leafy trees and of river willows, and celebrate before the Lord your God for seven days.
23.41: You are to hold this festival to honor the Lord for seven days every year .This regulation is for all time and for all future generations.
23.42: You are to live in temporary shelters for seven days. Every Israelite born in the country must live in shelters,
23.43: so that your descendants will remember that I made the Israelites live in shelters when I led them out of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.”
23.44: So Moses told the Israelites all about the Lord's festivals.

24.2: “Order the Israelites to bring you pure, pressed olive oil for the lamps, so they will always stay lit.
24.3: From evening until morning Aaron is to constantly look after the lamps before the Lord, outside the veil of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting. This regulation is for all time and for all future generations.
24.4: He is to constantly look after the lamps placed on the pure gold lampstand before the Lord.
24.5: Using the best flour bake twelve loaves, with two-tenths of an ephah of flour per loaf.
24.6: Place them in two piles, six in each pile, on the table made of pure gold that stands before the Lord.
24.7: Place pure frankincense beside each pile to go with the bread to act as the ‘reminder part,’ a food offering to the Lord.
24.8: Every Sabbath day the bread shall be placed before the Lord, given by the Israelites as an ongoing sign of the eternal agreement.
24.9: It is for Aaron and his descendants. They are to eat it in a holy place; for they must treat it as a most holy part of the food offerings given to the Lord. It is their share of the food offerings for all time.”
24.10: One day a man who had an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went into the Israelite camp and had a fight with an Israelite.
24.11: The Israelite woman's son cursed the name of the Lord. So they took him before Moses. (His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.)
24.12: They detained him until it was clear what the Lord wanted them to do about it.
24.14: “Take the man who cursed me outside the camp. Have all who heard him curse put their hands on his head; then have everyone stone him to death.
24.15: Tell the Israelites that anyone who curses their God will be punished for their sin.
24.16: Anyone who curses the name of the Lord must be executed. All of you must stone them to death, whether they are a foreigner who lives with you or an Israelite. If they curse my name, they must be executed.
24.17: Anyone who kills someone else must be executed.
24.18: Anyone who kills an animal has to replace it—a life for a life.
24.19: If anyone injures someone else, whatever they've done must be done to them:
24.20: a broken bone for a broken bone, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Whatever way they injured the victim, the same must be done to them.
24.21: Anyone who kills an animal has to replace it, but anyone who kills someone else must be executed.
24.22: The same laws apply to foreigners who live with you as to Israelites, for I am the Lord your God.”
24.23: Moses told this to the Israelites, and they took the man who cursed the Lord outside the camp and stoned him to death. The Israelites did what the Lord ordered Moses to do.

25.1: The Lord told Moses on Mount Sinai,
25.2: “Tell the Israelites: When you enter the land that I'm giving you, the land itself must also observe a Sabbath rest in honor of the Lord.
25.3: Six years you can cultivate your fields, take care of your vineyards, and harvest your crops.
25.4: But the seventh year is to be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath in honor of the Lord. Don't plant your fields or care for your vineyards.
25.5: Don't harvest what may have grown up in your fields, or collect the grapes from your vineyards that you haven't cared for .The land is to have a year of complete rest.
25.6: You can eat whatever the land produces during the Sabbath year .This applies to yourself, your male and female slaves, paid workers and foreigners who live with you,
25.7: and to your livestock and the wild animals living in your land. Whatever grows can be used for food.
25.8: Count seven ‘sabbaths’ of years, in other words, seven times seven years, so that the seven sabbaths of years come to forty-nine years.
25.9: Then blow the trumpet all through the country on the tenth day of the seventh month, which is the Day of Atonement. Make sure this signal is heard throughout your whole country.
25.10: You are to dedicate the fiftieth year and announce freedom everywhere in the country for all who live there. This is to be your Jubilee, when each of you is to return to reclaim your property and to be part of your family once more.
25.11: The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you. Don't sow the land; don't harvest what may have grown up in your fields, or collect the grapes from your vineyards that you haven't cared for .
25.12: It is a Jubilee and it is to be holy to you. You can eat whatever the land produces.
25.13: In this Jubilee Year ,every one of you shall return to your own property.
25.14: If you sell land to your neighbor ,or buy land from him, don't exploit one another .
25.15: When you buy from your neighbor work out how many years have passed since the last Jubilee, for he is to sell to you depending on how many years of harvest remain.
25.16: The more years that are left, the more you shall pay; the fewer years that are left, the less you shall pay, because he is actually selling you a specific number of harvests.
25.17: Don't exploit one another ,but have respect for your God, because I am the Lord your God.
25.18: Keep my rules and observe my regulations, so you can live in safety in the land. original owner ,and that anyone who had become a slave was set free and allowed to return to their own family.
25.19: Then the land will produce good harvests, so you will have plenty to eat and live in safety there.
25.20: But if you ask, ‘What are we going to do in the seventh year if we do not sow or harvest our crops?’
25.21: I will bless you in the sixth year ,so that the land will produce a crop that will be enough for three years.
25.22: As you sow in the eighth year ,you will still be eating from that harvest, which will last until your harvest in the ninth year .
25.23: Land must not be permanently sold, because it really belongs to me. To me you are only foreigners and travelers passing through.
25.24: So whatever land you buy to own, you must make arrangements so it can be returned to its original owner .
25.25: If one of your people becomes poor and sells you some of their land, their close family can come and buy back what they have sold.
25.26: However ,if they don't have anyone who can buy it back, but in the meantime their financial situation improves and they have enough to buy back the land,
25.27: they will work however many years it has been since the sale, and pay back the balance to the person who bought it, and go back to their property
25.28: If they can't raise enough to pay the person back for the land, the buyer will remain its owner until the Jubilee Year .But in the Jubilee Year the land will be returned so that the original owners can go back to their property.
25.29: If someone sells a house located in a walled town, they have the right to buy it back for a full year after selling it. It can be bought back any time during that year .
25.30: If it isn't bought back by the end of a full year ,then ownership of the house in the walled town is permanently transferred to the one who bought it and their descendants. It won't be returned in the Jubilee.
25.31: But houses in villages that don't have walls around them are to be treated as located in the fields. They can be bought back, and will be returned in the Jubilee.
25.32: However ,the Levites always have the right to buy back their houses in the towns that belong to them.
25.33: Whatever the Levites own can be bought back, even houses sold in their towns, and must be returned in the Jubilee. That's because the houses in the towns of the Levites are what they were given to own as their share among the Israelites.
25.34: However ,the fields surrounding their towns must not be sold because they belong to the Levites permanently.
25.35: If any of your people become poor and can't survive, you must help them in the same way you would help a foreigner or a stranger ,so that they can go on living in your neighborhood.
25.36: Don't make them pay you any interest or demand more than they borrowed, but respect your God so that they can remain living in your area.
25.37: Don't lend them silver with interest or sell them food at an inflated price.
25.38: Remember ,I am the Lord your God who led you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
25.39: If any of your people become poor and have to sell themselves to work for you, don't force them to work as a slave.
25.40: Have them live with you like a paid worker who is staying with you for a while. They are to work for you until the Jubilee Year .
25.41: Then they and their children must be freed, and they can go back to their family and to their family's property.
25.42: Israelites are not to be sold as slaves because they belong to me as my slaves—I led them out of Egypt.
25.43: Don't treat them with brutality. Have respect for your God.
25.44: Buy your male and female slaves from the surrounding nations.
25.45: You can also buy them from foreigners who have come to live among you, or from their descendants born in your land. You can treat them as your property.
25.46: You can pass them on to your children to inherit as property after you die. You can make them slaves for life, but you must not brutally treat any of your own people, the Israelites, as a slave.
25.47: If a foreigner among you becomes successful, and one of your people living nearby becomes poor and sells themselves to the foreigner or to a member of the foreigner's family,
25.48: they still have the right of being bought back after the sale. A member of their family can buy them back—
25.49: an uncle or cousin or any close relative from their family can buy them back. If they become successful, they can buy themselves back.
25.50: The person concerned and their buyer will work out the time from the year of the sale up to the Jubilee Year .The price will depend on the number of years, calculated using the daily rate for a paid worker .
25.51: If there are many years left, they must pay a larger percentage of the purchase price.
25.52: If there are only a few years remaining before the Jubilee Year ,then they only have to pay a percentage depending on the number of years still left.
25.53: They are to live with their foreign owner just like a paid worker ,hired from year to year ,but see to it that the owner doesn't treat him brutally.
25.54: If they are not bought back in any of the ways described, they and their children shall be freed in the Jubilee Year .
25.55: For the Israelites belong to me as my slaves. They are my slaves—I led them out of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.”

26.1: “Don't make yourselves idols anywhere in your land and bow down to worship them, whether they are images or sacred pillars or stone sculptures. For I am the Lord your God.
26.2: Keep my Sabbaths and show respect for my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
26.3: If you follow my rules and keep my regulations,
26.4: I will make sure it rains at the right time so that the ground will grow good crops and the fruit trees will be productive.
26.5: Your time of threshing will last right up to the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until the time you have to sow again. You will have more than enough to eat and you will live in safety in your land.
26.6: I will make sure your land is at peace. You will be able to sleep without being afraid of anything. I will get rid of dangerous animals from the land, and you will not suffer from any violent enemy attacks.
26.7: You will chase your enemies, and kill them with the sword.
26.8: Five of you will kill one hundred, and one hundred of you will kill ten thousand. You will destroy your enemies.
26.9: I will come to help you, so you will reproduce and increase in numbers, and I will confirm my agreement with you.
26.10: You'll still be eating your old stock of grain when you need to get rid of it so you can store the new grain.
26.11: I will come and live with you—I certainly won't reject you.
26.12: I shall always be right there with you. I will be your God, and you will be my people.
26.13: I am the Lord your God, who led you out of Egypt so you wouldn't have to be slaves to the Egyptians any longer .I smashed the yoke that kept you bent down and helped you to stand up straight.
26.14: But if you don't pay attention to me and do what I tell you;
26.15: if you reject my laws, hate my regulations, and refuse to follow my commandments, and consequently break my agreement,
26.16: then this is what I am going to do to you: I will make you panic, and suffer from diseases like tuberculosis and fever that make you blind and drain your life away. It will be pointless for you to sow seed in your fields because your enemies will eat the harvest.
26.17: I will turn against you, and you'll be defeated by your enemies. People who hate you will rule over you, and you'll run away even when there's no one chasing you!
26.18: If after all this you still refuse to obey me, I will move to punishing you seven times over for your sins.
26.19: I will break your self-reliant strength you're so proud of, and make your sky hard as iron and your land hard as bronze.
26.20: Your strength will be completely wasted because your land won't produce crops, and your trees won't produce fruit.
26.21: If you go on opposing me and refusing to do what I tell you, I will make your punishments seven times worse, based on your sins.
26.22: I will send wild animals to kill your children, wipe out your livestock, and make you so few in number that there won't be anyone on your roads.
26.23: However ,if in spite of all this correction you still don't change but go on opposing me,
26.24: then I will take action against you. I will punish you seven times over for your sins.
26.25: I will send enemies with swords to attack you in retaliation for breaking the agreement. Even though you retreat into your towns for defense, I will plague you with disease, and you will be handed over to your enemies.
26.26: I will send a famine so bread is in short supply. One oven will serve the needs of ten women baking bread. It will be distributed by weight so that you'll eat but won't have enough.
26.27: However ,if in spite of all this you don't obey me, but go on opposing me,
26.28: then I will take action against you in a rage of fury, and I will punish you myself seven times over for your sins.
26.29: You will eat the bodies of your own sons and daughters.
26.30: I will destroy your high places of worship, smash your altars of incense, and pile up your dead bodies on what remains of your idols, which also have no life at all. I will really despise you.
26.31: I will demolish your towns and destroy your pagan sanctuaries, and I will refuse to accept your sacrifices.
26.32: I will devastate your land myself, so that your enemies who come and live in it will be horrified at what has happened.
26.33: I'm going to scatter you among the nations. You will be chased out by armies with swords as your land is ruined and your towns are destroyed.
26.34: At least then the land will be able to enjoy its Sabbaths all the time it's abandoned while you are in exile in the land of your enemies. The land will finally be able to rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
26.35: The whole time it's abandoned the land will observe the Sabbaths of rest that it wasn't able to do while you were living there.
26.36: I will make those of you who survive so discouraged that as you live in the lands of your enemies even the sound of a leaf blowing in the wind will scare you into running away! You'll run away like you're being chased by someone with a sword, and fall down even though no one is after you.
26.37: You'll trip over each other as you run away from the attack, even though no one's there. You'll have no power to resist your enemies.
26.38: You'll die in exile and you'll be buried in a foreign country.
26.39: Those of you who do manage to survive in the countries of your enemies will wither away because of their guilt, decaying as they share the sins of their fathers.
26.40: They need to confess their sins and those of their fathers, acting in such an unfaithful way towards me, opposing me.
26.41: Because of this I took action against them and exiled them in the countries of their enemies. However ,if they humbly give up their stubborn attitude and accept their punishment for their sins,
26.42: then I will fulfill the agreement I made with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, and I will not forget my promise about the land.
26.43: For the land will be left empty by them, and it will enjoy its Sabbaths being abandoned. They will pay for their sins, because they rejected my rules and regulations.
26.44: But despite all this, even while they are living in land of their enemies, I will not reject or hate them so much as to destroy them and break my agreement with them, because I am the Lord their God.
26.45: Because of them I will renew the agreement I made with their fathers, those I led out of Egypt as the other nations watched, in order that I might be their God. I am the Lord.”
26.46: These are the rules, regulations, and laws that the Lord set up between himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.

27.2: “Tell the Israelites: When you make a special promise to dedicate someone to the Lord, these are the values you are to use.
27.3: The value of a man aged twenty to sixty is fifty shekels of silver (using the sanctuary shekel standard).
27.4: The value of a woman is thirty shekels.
27.5: The value of someone aged five to twenty is twenty shekels for a male and ten shekels for a female. properly observed.
27.6: The value of someone aged one month to five years is five shekels of silver for a male and three shekels of silver for a female.
27.7: The value of someone aged sixty or older is fifteen shekels for a male and ten shekels of silver for a female.
27.8: However ,if when you fulfill your promise you are poorer than the fixed value, you are to present the person before the priest, who will then set the value depending on what you can afford.
27.9: If when you fulfill your promise you bring an animal that is permitted as an offering to the Lord, the animal given to the Lord shall be considered holy.
27.10: You are not allowed to replace it or swap it, either for one that is better or one that is worse. However ,if you do replace it then both animals become holy.
27.11: If when you fulfill your promise you bring any unclean animal that is not permitted as an offering to the Lord, then you must show the animal to the priest.
27.12: The priest will decide its value, whether high or low. Whatever value the priest places on it is final.
27.13: If you then decide to buy the animal back, you have to add one-fifth to its value in payment.
27.14: If you dedicate your house as holy to the Lord, then the priest will decide its value, whether high or low. Whatever value the priest places on it remains final.
27.15: But if you want to buy back your house, you have to add one-fifth to its value in payment. Then it will belong to you again.
27.16: If you dedicate some of your land to the Lord, then its value shall be determined by the amount of seed required to sow it: fifty shekels of silver for every homer of barley seed used.
27.17: If you dedicate your field during the Jubilee Year ,the value will be the full amount calculated.
27.18: But if you dedicate your field after the Jubilee, the priest will work out the value depending on the number of years left until the next Jubilee Year ,so reducing the value.
27.19: But if you want to buy your field back, you have to add one-fifth to its value in payment. Then it will belong to you again.
27.20: But if you don't buy the field back, or if you've already sold it to someone else, it can't ever be bought back.
27.21: When the Jubilee comes, the field will become holy, in the same way as a field devoted to the Lord. It will become the property of the priests.
27.22: If you dedicate to the Lord a field you've bought that was not part of your original property,
27.23: the priest will work out the value until the next Jubilee Year .You will pay on that day the exact value, giving it as a holy offering to the Lord.
27.24: In the Jubilee Year ,ownership of the field shall revert back to the person you bought it from—to the original owner of the land.
27.25: (All values will use the sanctuary shekel standard of twenty gerahs to the shekel.)
27.26: No one is allowed to dedicate the firstborn of the livestock, because the firstborn belongs to the Lord. Whether they are cattle, sheep, or goats, they are the Lord's.
27.27: But if it is an unclean animal, then you can buy it back according to its value, adding on one-fifth extra. If it's not bought back, then it is to be sold according to its value.
27.28: Anything that you specially dedicate to the Lord from what you own, whether (set apart), either by destroying them or presenting them as an offering. it's a person, an animal, or your land, can't be sold or bought back. Anything specially dedicated is most holy to the Lord.
27.29: No one who is specially dedicated to destruction can be bought back. They must be killed.
27.30: Tithe from your crops or fruit belongs to the Lord; it is holy to the Lord.
27.31: If you want to buy back some of your tithe, you must add on one-fifth to its value.
27.32: When you count your herds and flocks, every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd's rod is holy to the Lord.
27.33: You must not examine it to see if it's good or bad, and you must not replace it. However ,if you do replace it then both animals become holy; they can't be bought back.”
27.34: These are the laws the Lord gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
